what_breaks: F-15 is only half closed. After a storage failure on the new order or edit order form, focus moves to the banner and stays there, so Save is not ready for a retry. The customer form was fixed; the order form was not.
evidence: order-form.js:199 commit(result.data) fails on a full quota, :201 showBanner(saved.code), :202 return, with no Save focus. main.js:121 runs setBanner(region, ...).focus(). customer-form.js:112-113 has the fix: showBanner, then form.querySelector('[type="submit"]').focus(). UI-SPEC.md:502: 'Failed Save, storage | stays on Save, ready to retry'. F-15 named both forms, and neither the S11 nor the S14 commit changed this path. MANUAL-CHECKS.md:108 checks the kept form and STO-01 but not focus, so nothing catches it.

what_breaks: F-43 is closed for one of the two search boxes. Deleting a customer clears the customer search but not the order search. A name typed there to find that customer's orders stays in the Search orders box after the app has said all of this customer's data is erased, until a reload.
evidence: Type 'Ion' in Search orders: order-list.js:127 sets state.searchOrders = 'Ion'. Delete Ion's orders and then Ion. main.js:100 customerWasDeleted(nextData) is true but clears only state.searchCustomers. With any other customer's order left, renderOrderList takes buildList, and order-list.js:96 sets input.value = state.searchOrders, so 'Ion' is shown. R-10 searches customer name, so this box does hold names. eraseAll at main.js:181-182 clears both boxes, so the delete path is the odd one out.

what_breaks: Some invisible characters still count as text in a required field, so a customer or a line can be saved with nothing visible. A customer whose name is only U+034F then gets a list row link with no visible text to click.
evidence: INVISIBLE_ONLY is /^[\p{Cf}\p{Z}\s]*$/u. U+034F combining grapheme joiner and U+FE0F variation selector are zero-width with category Mn. U+3164 and U+115F Hangul fillers are Lo. U+0001 is Cc. None is in Cf, Z or \s, and String.trim keeps them. For name = U+034F, validation.js:43 test is false, length 1 passes the 1 to 100 check at :44, and validateCustomer returns ok. customer-list.js:32 then renders a link with no visible text. R-17 says zero-width or other format characters count as empty. tests/validation.test.js:186 and :193 use only Cf characters, so a stricter rule is untested. Severity is advisory because reaching it takes pasting an unusual code point and no data is lost.

what_breaks: F-10 is closed off by one. With nextOrderNumber at the largest value the shape accepts, creating one order writes a document the same check refuses on the next load, so readable data becomes blocked as corrupt. Only a hand-edited document can reach this.
evidence: Stored nextOrderNumber = 9007199254740990: shape.js:91 isSafeInteger(value) and isSafeInteger(value + 1 = 9007199254740991) are both true, so it loads. orders.js:44 writes nextOrderNumber 9007199254740991, and storage.js:50 saves it. On reload shape.js:91 sees value + 1 = 2^53, which is not safe, so hasValidCounter is false and storage.js:23 returns corrupt. tests/shape.test.js:90 pins only MAX_SAFE_INTEGER as refused, and no test covers the step below it.

what_breaks: F-47 is fixed for the Customer field only. The edit order form still labels the read-only order number as Number (optional), the same wording the human rejected for a fixed value.
evidence: order-form.js:85-91 calls field({ id: 'order-number', label: 'Number', required: false, control: readOnlyInput(...) }). components.js:76 builds the text `${spec.label} (${spec.required ? 'required' : 'optional'})`, which gives 'Number (optional)'. customerField at order-form.js:75 overrides the label to 'Customer', and no such override exists for Number. decisions.json UAT-2: 'must not call a fixed value optional'.

what_breaks: Both search-clearing rules in commit have no test and no manual check. Removing the whole condition at main.js:100 would break the R-01 clause (F-07) and F-43, and no test or listed check would notice.
evidence: main.js:100 is the only code for 'a customer search kept from before is cleared'. ADR-003 leaves views and main.js to manual checks. The R-01 line, MANUAL-CHECKS.md:63, says only 'save a name only, the customer appears in the list', with no prior search. The R-04 line, :84, says nothing about the search. A grep for 'search' in MANUAL-CHECKS.md hits only lines 45, 47, 60, 166, 167, 169 and 180, and none covers saving a new customer or deleting one. No file under tests/ can import main.js because it runs start() against the DOM at load.

what_breaks: Suspicion: the email control is type=email, and Chromium may return an internationalised domain as punycode in .value. The stored email would then differ from what was typed, and the list and a search on the typed domain would not match it.
evidence: customer-form.js:12 sets type 'email' (UI-SPEC.md:210 asks for it) and :31 reads form.elements.email.value. No browser was run, so the conversion is unconfirmed. To settle it, run a manual check in Chrome: save a customer with email ion@exämple.ro, then read the customer list and search for exämple.

what_breaks: The F-13 fix covers only part of R-17. INVISIBLE_ONLY matches categories Cf and Z and whitespace, so a zero-width character of another category still counts as text. A customer name or line description made only of such a character is saved with no visible text.
evidence: Input: paste U+FE0F (variation selector-16, zero width, Unicode category Mn) as the customer name. textOf (validation.js:34) keeps it because trim() removes only whitespace. lengthError (:43) tests /^[\p{Cf}\p{Z}\s]*$/u, which does not match Mn, so it passes. Length is 1, createCustomer stores it, and the h1 and list link have no visible text. The picker shows only ' (no email)'. U+034F and U+E0100 (both Mn, zero width) take the same path, and so does a line description (:111). Tests at validation.test.js:186 and :193 use only Cf and Z characters. Similar blanks that R-17 does not literally name, U+3164 (Lo), U+2800 (So) and U+0001 (Cc), also pass; whether they count is for the human. The regex path was read, not run; the categories come from the Unicode data. The verifier can settle it with a test on validateCustomer({ name: '\uFE0F' }).

what_breaks: The email check tests length only, so invisible text on either side of the @ counts as text. An optional email with nothing visible before the @ is stored, despite the R-01 rule of text on both sides.
evidence: Input: email U+200B followed by @b.c. trim() keeps U+200B, split gives ['\u200B','b.c'], parts[0].length is 1 and parts[1] has a dot, so emailError returns null and the value is stored. It displays as @b.c. a@ followed by U+200B and a dot passes the same way. INVISIBLE_ONLY runs only in lengthError for required fields, not in emailError. Advisory because R-17 names required fields only and the email is optional. No test feeds this input.

what_breaks: The fix for SEC-3 is one short at the top of the counter. A stored nextOrderNumber one below the highest value the check accepts passes on load, but creating one order then writes a document the app refuses on the next load, so readable data becomes blocked as corrupt.
evidence: Input: a valid document with "nextOrderNumber":9007199254740990. hasValidCounter passes because value + 1 is 9007199254740991, which is safe, and load returns ok. createOrder (orders.js:44) saves nextOrderNumber 9007199254740991 with order ORD-9007199254740990. On reload value + 1 is 9007199254740992, which is not safe, so hasValidCounter is false, hasValidShape is false and load returns corrupt. Hand-edited data only, since the app cannot reach this counter by itself.

what_breaks: F-33 is not closed although commit f19ef9e says it is. The app now supplies `today`, but nothing in src reads it. The only live clock is still `deps.now`, called from the view.
evidence: ADR-003 line 31: '`deps` carries what the outside supplies, `newId` and `today`'. Code: order-form.js:160 `todayIso(deps.now)`; main.js:74 '`now` stays for views that still read the clock'; main.js:77 `now: () => Date.now(),`. A grep for deps.today under src/ finds nothing. Commit f19ef9e: 'F-16, F-21, F-33, F-36, F-23..F-27 already closed in shared files'.

what_breaks: F-36 is not closed for the order form. It calls commit without a hash and then navigates itself, so the one write path of ADR-003 is still split. The target can be computed from result.data before the commit, as customer-form.js does with its own target.
evidence: ADR-003 line 32: '`commit` calls `storage.save(result.data)`; only when that succeeds does it replace the state, navigate and render.' Code: order-form.js:199 `const saved = commit(result.data);`, then :204-205 `state.form = null; location.hash = savedHash(route, result.data);`. F-36's evidence named this exact call site (order-form.js:203). customer-form.js:110 uses `commit(result.data, where.saved)`. Commit f19ef9e lists F-36 as 'already closed in shared files'.

what_breaks: F-15 is fixed only on the customer form. After a failed storage save on the order form, focus still moves to the banner, not to Save.
evidence: UI-SPEC line 502: 'Failed Save, storage | stays on Save, ready to retry'. Code: order-form.js:201 `showBanner(saved.code);` then `return;`, and main.js:121 `return setBanner(region, bannerFor(code)).focus();`. F-15's what_breaks says 'the customer or order form' and its evidence names order-form.js:199. customer-form.js:113 got `form.querySelector('[type="submit"]').focus();`; order-form.js did not. F-15 was routed to S11 only, so S14 never received it.

what_breaks: F-34 is fixed in one of the three views. order-list.js and order-view.js still read the browser locale themselves, and they ignore the `locale` the composition root now passes.
evidence: ADR-006 line 24: 'The locale is `navigator.language`, read once in `src/ui/main.js` and passed as an argument'. Code: order-list.js:105 and order-view.js:199 `const locale = navigator.language;`. main.js:212 passes `locale: LOCALE`, which only customer-detail.js:132 takes. Commit 6e0f818 changed order-view.js and left line 199 as it was.

what_breaks: F-35 is reported closed by commits 6e0f818 and eba225d, but only the listeners of order-view.js changed. Views still take one context object holding the whole mutable state, they write state directly, and other views keep per-control listeners.
evidence: ADR-003 line 35: 'A view has the shape `render(container, viewModel, actions)` and one delegated listener per container'. Code: order-view.js:194 `export function renderOrderView(container, context)`, :195 destructures `state`, :251 `state.form = { hash: location.hash, ...`. customer-form.js:119 and order-form.js:210 do the same. customer-detail.js:145 and :154 and customer-list.js:65 and :73 attach per-button listeners. F-35's text names all three parts: context object, listeners, direct writes to state.

what_breaks: F-43 is half closed. Deleting a customer clears the customer search but not the order search. R-04 tells the user to delete the orders first, and the natural way to find them is typing the customer's name into Search orders, so that name stays in the box after the customer's data is erased.
evidence: Cycle 1 LEG-1: 'with no reset of state.searchCustomers or state.searchOrders'. F-43: 'the same reset eraseAll does would close the gap'. Code: main.js:100 resets only `state.searchCustomers`; eraseAll at main.js:181-182 resets both; order-list.js:96 `input.value = state.searchOrders;` restores the text. R-04: 'deleting those orders (R-08) and then the customer erases all of this customer's data'.

what_breaks: The F-39 fix still does not follow the decision: formatDate never calls Date.UTC. The rewrite also adds handling and a test for years 0000 to 0099, inputs the human rejected as not real in F-29, so this is behaviour nothing asks for.
evidence: ADR-007 line 45: 'built with `Date.UTC` and formatted with `timeZone: 'UTC'`'. Code: format.js:17-18 `const date = new Date(0); date.setUTCFullYear(year, month - 1, day);`. tests/format.test.js:33 `R-28 formatDate shows 0099-01-01 as year 99`. docs/review/1/decisions.json note: 'F-29: years 0000 to 0099 are not a real input.' The shown day is right for every real date.

what_breaks: The assertion cannot catch the defect its title names. If formatDate used Date.UTC, year 99 would become 1999, and '1 Jan 1999' still includes '99'. Advisory because the test's other line can fail and the input is one the human ruled out in F-29.
evidence: Test title: 'R-28 formatDate shows 0099-01-01 as year 99'. Assertion: `assert.equal(formatDate('0099-01-01', 'en-GB').includes('99'), true);`. Date.UTC maps years 0 to 99 onto 1900 to 1999, the reason dates.js:9 calls setUTCFullYear. AGENTS.md rule 2: 'A test must be able to fail'. Replacing format.js:17-18 with `new Date(Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day))` passes this assertion.

what_breaks: F-32 is half closed. The S3 half was fixed, but the S6 half is unchanged: the builder's export test still checks fragments of A-13 and A-14, and tests/export.test.js is in no fix commit. Only the tester's spec holds the full texts.
evidence: PLAN line 164: `R-29 buildCustomerExport states the purpose of A-13, the retention of A-14 and the currency EUR`. Code: export.test.js:19 `assert.ok(result.purpose.endsWith('The data is used for nothing else.'));`, :20 `assert.ok(result.retention.includes('there is no fixed period'));`. F-32: 'the export test checks only fragments of A-13 and A-14'. F-32 was routed to S3 only, whose Files line does not hold this test. tests/export.spec.mjs:77-92 hold the stronger checks.

what_breaks: Two builder tests assert a value that the empty default already gives. The R-19 round trip would pass if save wrote nothing, because load of an empty backing returns the same object. The R-06 erase test never raises the counter, so it proves no restart. Advisory because other tests catch both defects (storage.test.js:68 and the specs).
evidence: tests/storage.test.js:14 `const data = { nextOrderNumber: 1, customers: [], orders: [] };`, :21 `assert.deepEqual(createStorage(backing).load(), { ok: true, data });`; storage.js:6 and :40 return that value for a missing key. tests/storage.test.js:46-50: `createStorage(memory())`, then `assert.equal(storage.erase().data.nextOrderNumber, 1);`. PLAN lines 182 and 199 name a saved-data round trip and a restart. tests/storage.spec.mjs:79 and :532 use real documents.

what_breaks: The R-01 clause added after review (a kept search is cleared on create) has no test and no manual check, the same gap F-44 closed for R-31. Nothing would catch a regression. The same holds for the F-43 clearing after a customer delete.
evidence: R-01: 'a customer search kept from before is cleared so the new customer is visible (review F-07)'. Code exists at main.js:100, which cannot run under Node (ADR-001). MANUAL-CHECKS.md:63 and PLAN line 342: 'save a name only, the customer appears in the list; save with email ab.c, the error shows and nothing is saved', with no search step. Grep for 'cleared' and 'search kept' in both files finds no such line. AGENTS.md Definition of done: 'listed for a manual check (UI)'.

what_breaks: The invisible-text rule lives in R-17, but its tests carry R-01 and R-11, so a trace of R-17 misses it. The plan's S2 Tests first list was not updated for the new criterion, and the fix commit does not name R-17.
evidence: R-17: 'A text made only of invisible characters (zero-width or other format characters) counts as empty for every required field (review F-13).' Tests: validation.test.js:186 `R-01 a customer name made only of invisible characters...`, :193 `R-11 a line description made only of invisible characters...`. AGENTS.md rule 4: 'Every requirement you implement is named in a test title'. Commit 4791fde: 'S2: fix F-03, F-13 (R-01, R-11)'. PLAN S2 Tests first (lines 43-58) has no such title.

what_breaks: On order edit the read-only Number field is labelled `Number (optional)`. This is the same complaint the human raised in UAT on the read-only Customer field, and the fix covered Customer only. Read 1: F-47 applies to every fixed value, so the label must lose the suffix. Read 2: the approved spec row gives Required 'no', so `(optional)` follows the spec.
evidence: decisions.json F-47: 'the label must say Customer and not call a fixed value optional'. Code: order-form.js:85-91 `field({ id: 'order-number', label: 'Number', required: false, ...`, and components.js:76 appends ' (optional)'. Only the customer label is overwritten, at order-form.js:75. UI-SPEC line 83: label 'with ` (required)` or ` (optional)` as part of the label text'; line 354: Number, Required `no`. Settled by the human saying whether F-47 covers Number.

what_breaks: The blocked screen puts the h1 above the panel, while the section 7.8 sketch has the heading inside it.
evidence: UI-SPEC lines 470-477: the box holds '| | The saved data cannot    | |' above 'Nothing has been changed.' and the buttons, under 'Invoice app'. Line 458: 'only the text `Invoice app` as in the header, then a panel of width `--width-form`'. Code: blocked.js:68 `container.replaceChildren(element('p', 'app-name', 'Invoice app'), h1, box);`, and box holds only the region, the text and the actions (line 54).

what_breaks: The two not-found links are drawn as bordered secondary buttons, not the link variant the spec names.
evidence: UI-SPEC line 442: 'then link buttons `Go to customers` and `Go to orders`'. Sketch lines 450-451 show them without the [ ] used for buttons. Line 422 uses the same words for Edit and Remove, which order-view.js:68 builds as `actionButton('Edit', 'link', ...)`. Code: not-found.js:9 `linkButton('Go to customers', '#/customers', 'secondary'), linkButton('Go to orders', '#/orders', 'secondary')`.

what_breaks: On desktop the Order total label sits at the far left of the row, away from its amount. The spec places the line at the end of the row.
evidence: UI-SPEC line 424: 'Order total: one line under the table ... at the end of the row'. Sketch line 417: '|                                        Order total     €59.97  |'. Code: `.order-total { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; ...}`, with no change at 64rem. The 320 px sketch (line 401) does spread the two.

what_breaks: The action cell of a line row keeps its vertical padding on desktop, so rows grow to about 60 px, not --row-height.
evidence: UI-SPEC line 422: 'its vertical padding is 0, so the row stays at `--row-height`'. Code: styles.css:631 sets `padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-3);` on every `.table-lines td`, with no override for `.col-actions`. `.button` keeps `height: var(--control-height)` (line 175), and `.row-actions .button` (line 596) changes only the side padding.

what_breaks: A banner action stays on the text's row at 320 px and squeezes the text. The spec puts it below the text. The F-27 change made the text's flex basis 0, so the wrap never happens. This affects STO-05, APP-01 and the copy-failure banner.
evidence: UI-SPEC line 89: 'at most one action as a link button at the end (below the text at 320 px)'. Code: styles.css:255 `flex-wrap: wrap;`, line 265 `.banner-text { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }`, and no media rule for banners. With basis 0 the icon, the text and the action always fit on one flex line.

what_breaks: A long customer name in the h1 of the customer detail has no wrap rule, so a 100-character name with no spaces overflows at 320 px and gives horizontal scroll.
evidence: UI-SPEC line 65: 'every text from the user wraps with `overflow-wrap: anywhere`, except the desktop table cells'. Line 249: 'h1: the customer's name'. Code: styles.css:91-92 set only weight, line height, margin and size on h1. customer-detail.js:138 `heading(customer.name)`. Grep finds no h1 or `.title-row` rule with overflow-wrap.

what_breaks: The blocked screen's title sits in main.js, outside the frozen table of titles, and no test checks it. Read 1: the plan's table covers all of section 7, so it belongs in router.js. Read 2: ADR-005's table holds route names and the blocked screen is not a route, so main.js is fine.
evidence: PLAN line 229: 'the frozen table of page titles of UI-SPEC section 7 in `src/ui/router.js`'. UI-SPEC line 458 is in section 7: 'Page title: `Data problem - Invoice app`'. ADR-005 line 45: 'a frozen table of route names'. Code: main.js:58 `const BLOCKED_TITLE = 'Data problem - Invoice app';`. ROUTE_TITLES in router.js has no such entry. Settled by the human saying which reading holds.

what_breaks: Two documents the decisions rely on are missing: the runbook lines for the error codes and the trace file. No slice in the plan writes either, so they may belong to the delivery step. This adds to LEG-5, which covered only the T-02 line.
evidence: ADR-007 line 27: 'each needs a line in `docs/RUNBOOK.md` (EO-13)'. ADR-002 line 36: '`docs/TRACE.md` links each requirement to its tests, commits and manual check.' `ls` reports both missing, and neither is on a Files line in PLAN.md. Settled by confirming that the devops role and the gate write them before release.

what_breaks: The F-43 fix clears only the customer search. A customer name typed into the order search stays in the box after that customer is deleted, until a reload.
evidence: Rule: LD-07 'The person can have their personal data erased'; reviewer question: 'Does a delete leave a copy under another key, in a cache or in an index'. Code: main.js:100 'if (state.route?.name === 'customer-new' || customerWasDeleted(nextData)) state.searchCustomers = '';', with no reset of state.searchOrders. Only eraseAll (main.js:182) resets it. R-10 makes the order search match customer names, and order-list.js:96 'input.value = state.searchOrders' puts the text back. Path: with a second customer who has an order, type 'Jane' in the order search, open Jane's only order and delete it, then delete Jane from her customer detail and open Orders. The box shows 'Jane' with 'No orders match this search.', although the banner at customer-detail.js:100 promised 'all of this customer's data is erased'. Limits: memory only, nothing in localStorage, gone on reload. Same class as F-43.

what_breaks: The F-43 fix has no test and no manual check, so removing the search reset after a customer delete would go unnoticed.
evidence: Rule: LD-07; reviewer question: 'Is there a test per rule the slice touches whose assertion fails if the rule is broken?'. Code: customerWasDeleted in src/ui/main.js:106-109 carries the comment 'R-04: once a customer is deleted, the text typed to find them is cleared too'. main.js cannot run under Node (ADR-001), so a manual line is the available cover. MANUAL-CHECKS.md lines 83-84, the R-04 checks, end at 'confirming deletes it and lands on the list' and neither involves a search. A search for F-43 in docs/MANUAL-CHECKS.md and docs/PLAN.md finds nothing. Path: drop customerWasDeleted from main.js:100; no test fails and no listed check notices. F-44 was the same gap for R-31 and was accepted.

what_breaks: After a customer's name or email is corrected, the old value stays in the customer or order search box if it was typed there to find them. No save other than a new customer or a delete clears it.
evidence: Rule: LD-04 'Personal data can be corrected, and the correction reaches every place it is shown'. Code: main.js:100 clears searchCustomers only on customer-new or a delete, so an update leaves both search texts. Path: search 'Jane Smiht', open her, correct the name to 'Jane Smith', save, return to Customers: the box shows 'Jane Smiht' and 'No customers match this search.'. Reading A: a search box is what the user typed, not a place the app shows customer data, and ADR-005 line 46 says search texts 'survive moving between screens', so LD-04 is met. Reading B: the accepted F-43 treated the same text as a copy of a person's data, and the rule's Why names 'a copy left in a cache' as inaccurate data the app still keeps. Settled by the human saying whether the F-43 reading extends to rectification.

what_breaks: Carried from cycle 1 LEG-2, unchanged and not answered: the export's purpose and retention texts carry project ids and backticked field names the person receiving the file cannot look up.
evidence: Rule: LD-06 'The person can obtain a copy of their personal data', with 'which data is held, for what purpose, how long'. Code: export.js:5 'the user applies this rule with R-04 and R-08. No legal retention applies while the app issues no invoices (A-10).'. Reading A: ADR-007 freezes these texts from A-13 and A-14 and R-29 asks the file to state them, so it complies. Reading B: R-29 says 'the user can answer a person's access request with this one file', and that person has no docs/REQUIREMENTS.md. docs/review/1/decisions.json holds no answer. Settled by the human: the frozen texts stay, or a plain-language version in an accepted ADR.

what_breaks: Carried from cycle 1 LEG-3, unchanged and not answered: A-13 says notes and line description should hold no details about other people, but only the notes field carries the warning.
evidence: Rule: LD-03 'The app stores only the personal data its purpose needs, by default'. A-13: 'notes and line description record what the order is about and should not hold details about other people'. Code: order-form.js:8 NOTES_HELPER carries the warning; order-view.js:155 gives Description no helper. Reading A: UI-SPEC line 432, approved, sets the helper to 'none', so the build matches the spec. Reading B: the safeguard A-13 states for both fields reaches only one. Settled by the human saying whether UI-SPEC line 432 stands.

what_breaks: Carried from cycle 1 LEG-4, unchanged and not answered: an order's customerId, listed as personal data, is corrected only by deleting and rebuilding the order, which retypes every line and uses up a number.
evidence: Rule: LD-04 'Personal data can be corrected'. Code: validation.js:94-97 validateOrderEdit takes date and notes only; order-form.js:73 'To move an order, delete it and create a new one.'. Reading A: A-06, confirmed by the human, makes this the accepted correction path. Reading B: the cost fails 'without undue delay' in the rule's Why. Settled by the human confirming A-06 under LD-04 in docs/decisions, or asking for a move command.

what_breaks: Carried from cycle 1 LEG-5, unchanged and not answered: the accepted answer to threat T-02 rests on a runbook that does not exist, and the app's note says nothing about the shared github.io origin.
evidence: Rule: LD-09 'Personal data does not leak into logs, error messages, URLs or the storage of a shared machine'. ADR-008 line 46: 'anyone who keeps real customer data runs the app from localhost or from an origin of their own. The runbook says so.'. Check: docs/RUNBOOK.md is absent, .github/workflows holds only gate.yml, and customer-list.js:5 says only 'Your data lives only in this browser'. Nothing is published, so no user reaches this today. Settled by the devops role adding the runbook before the first publish, and the human saying whether the published app shows a demo-only note.

what_breaks: Carried from cycle 1 LEG-7, unchanged and not answered: two GitHub actions used in CI are named in no decision with an SPDX identifier, while ADR-001 says the project has no development dependencies.
evidence: Rule: LL-01 'Every third-party component is named with its SPDX licence identifier'. Code: gate.yml:15 and :20 'uses: actions/checkout@v7', :27 'uses: actions/setup-node@v7'. ADR-001: 'Dependencies: none, neither runtime nor development'. Limits: they run only in CI and are not shipped, and A-15 names only 'library, font, icon set or adapted design'. Settled by the human saying whether CI actions count as components under LL-01; if so, a decision names them with the SPDX ids read from each repository.
